@context._vocab_note: Feature terms (place, manner, voiced, height, backness, rounded, tense, lateral, strident, affricate, tract) are our CC-BY facts; they ALIGN to CLTS feature parameters and PanPhon feature names (see _meta.alignsWith). Per-term IRI mapping to CLTS is a follow-up; a canonical @context URL is a follow-up.

_meta.title: Articulation — how each English sound is made and FELT
_meta.description: Place x Manner x Voicing for consonants and, for vowels, tongue Height x Backness x Rounding x Tenseness, plus formant/vocal-tract synth hints and a plain 'how a child feels it' cue for the multisensory teaching layer. Shared facts of articulatory phonetics (not any program's materials).
_meta.source_notes: Consonant place/manner/voicing: ASHA chart + standard phonetics. Vowel height/backness/rounding/tense: the IPA vowel quadrilateral (textbook fact). Nominal formant values: Klatt/Peterson-Barney adult-male norms. Multisensory 'feel it' pedagogy: Ehri lab (mouth pictures), visible-mouth study, Lindamood/LiPS tradition (cited, NOT reproduced). See docs/articulatory-features-review.md.
_meta.validation: Mechanically checked against PanPhon (MIT) and alignable to CLTS (CC-BY) by tools/validate-articulation-panphon.py. Tenseness of low vowels (ae, a) is theory-dependent — expect benign mismatches there, like glottal /h/ for manner.
_meta.synthContract: The 'tract' + 'formants' fields are the control-parameter contract for a separate MIT articulatory-synth project: backness->Pink Trombone tongueIndex, height->tongueDiameter, rounded->lip; height~inverse F1, backness~F2 for Klatt/klattsch.
_meta.note: Consonants keyed by common grapheme; vowelPhonemes keyed by IPA. Sounds are properties of PHONEMES; a decoder maps grapheme->phoneme first (see phonologicalPatterns.json).

voicingTest: Put a hand on your throat: VOICED sounds buzz (b, z, m), VOICELESS sounds don't (p, s, t).

mannerFeel.stop: a closure then a release — the air is blocked, then pops out (p, t, k, b, d, g)
mannerFeel.nasal: air comes out the NOSE — pinch your nose and the sound stops (m, n, ng)
mannerFeel.fricative: a long, continuous hiss or buzz — the air squeezes through (f, s, sh, th, v, z)
mannerFeel.affricate: a stop THEN a fricative, joined — a tap then a hiss (ch, j)
mannerFeel.liquid: the tongue glides and the air flows around it (l, r)
mannerFeel.glide: the mouth slides toward the next vowel (w, y)

p.feel: lips press together, then pop apart — no throat buzz

t.feel: tongue tip taps behind the top teeth — no buzz

d.feel: tongue tip taps the ridge — throat buzzes

k.feel: back of the tongue lifts to the roof — no buzz

g.feel: back of the tongue lifts — throat buzzes

m.feel: lips closed, humming out the nose

n.feel: tongue tip up, humming out the nose

ng.feel: back of tongue up, humming out the nose

f.feel: top teeth on the bottom lip, air hisses out

s.feel: air hisses over the tongue tip — a snake sound

z.feel: a buzzing hiss — a bee sound

sh.feel: quiet 'shh' air, lips a little round

th.feel: tongue between the teeth, air out (thin)

h.feel: a soft puff from the throat

ch.feel: a tap then a 'shh' — like a sneeze

l.feel: tongue tip up, air slides around the sides

r.feel: tongue pulls back and bunches — nothing touches

w.feel: lips round, then slide to the vowel

y.feel: tongue high, then slides to the vowel

vowels._note: Vowels are 'open' sounds — the voice is on and the air flows freely; you feel them in the JAW (how far it drops), the TONGUE (high/low, front/back), and the LIPS (round or not). Per-phoneme detail is in vowelPhonemes; short/long below is the classroom grouping.

short.feel: a quick, relaxed (lax) sound — the jaw and tongue stay loose

long.feel: the vowel 'says its name' — a longer, tenser sound

feelExamples.ee: smile — lips spread wide, tongue high and front (see)
feelExamples.ah: drop the jaw wide open, tongue low (father)
feelExamples.oo: round the lips into a tunnel (moon)

i.feel: tongue high and forward, lips spread in a smile — a long, bright sound (see)

\u026a.feel: like /i/ but relaxed — tongue drops a little, jaw loose (sit)

\u025b.feel: tongue mid and forward, mouth a little open (bed)

\u00e6.feel: jaw drops low, tongue forward — mouth wide (cat)

\u0251.feel: jaw drops wide, tongue low and pulled back (father)

\u0252.feel: low and back with a little lip rounding (British hot)

\u028c.feel: a short, relaxed middle sound, mouth slightly open (cup)

\u028a.feel: tongue high and back, lips a little round — relaxed (book)

u.feel: tongue high and back, lips round into a tunnel — a long sound (moon)

\u0259.feel: the lazy middle sound — mouth barely moves (about)

e\u026a.feel: starts mid-front, glides up toward /i/ as the jaw closes (day)

o\u028a.feel: starts back, glides up and rounds toward /u/ (go)

a\u026a.feel: starts low and open, glides up to /i/ as the jaw closes (my)

a\u028a.feel: starts low and open, glides up and rounds (cow)

\u0254\u026a.feel: starts back and rounded, glides forward to /i/ (boy)
